title: How many cows do the two cowherds have?
description: Two cowherds meet on the road. One has twice as many cows as the other, and after three cows are given across, both have the same number. A letter gives two gee take away three equals gee plus three, so the cows are six and twelve.
teaching_notes: One idea: let a letter be the smaller herd, write the larger as twice that, then make the two herds equal after three cows move. Watch for students who take three from one herd but forget to add three to the other.

video_script.why: The child uses a letter for the unknown count and builds an equation by following a change, as in the sticker puzzle, then checks both herds.
video_script.substitution: Let g be the first herd, the second is 2g; after 3 move, 2g − 3 = g + 3, so g = 6 and the second herd is 12.
video_script.anchor: two cowherds on a road with their cows, three cows moving from the larger herd to the smaller one
video_script.payoff_line: {{NAME_3}} has six cows and {{NAME_4}} has twelve

final_answer.spoken: {{NAME_3}} has six cows and {{NAME_4}} has twelve

names.{{NAME_4}}: the cowherd with twice as many cows

maths_rules: let g be the cows of the first cowherd; the second has 2g
after giving 3: second has 2g − 3, first has g + 3
video_script.design: One idea: a letter for the smaller herd gives the larger herd as twice that, and moving three cows makes the two herds equal. The two herds stay on the board and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. {{NAME_3}} and {{NAME_4}} are cowherds who pass each other on the road.
<bookmark mark='says'/>{{NAME_3}} says that {{NAME_4}} has twice as many cows.
<bookmark mark='gives'/>{{NAME_4}} agrees, but if three cows were given to {{NAME_3}}, both would have the same number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many cows does each of them have on the road today?

beats.on_screen: the two herds stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: giving 3 away = take away 3; receiving 3 = plus 3; a letter g stands for the smaller herd

marks.move: take away 3 is marked on the giver and plus 3 on the receiver
marks.letter: a box with the letter g stands for the smaller herd

narration: <bookmark mark='move'/>The one who gives three cows has three fewer. The one who receives them has three more.
<bookmark mark='letter'/>We do not know the smaller herd, so a letter can stand for it.

beats.on_screen: Given: the larger herd is 2 times the smaller; after 3 cows move, both herds are equal
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_4}} has twice as many cows as {{NAME_3}}. After three cows move across, both have the same number.

beats.on_screen: To find: the cows each cowherd has

marks.find: the words cows of each cowherd are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many cows each of them has.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: let g = the cows of the smaller herd; the larger herd = 2g

marks.let: g is written as the smaller herd
marks.twice: 2g is written as the larger herd

narration: <bookmark mark='let'/>Step one, let gee be the number of cows {{NAME_3}} has.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>{{NAME_4}} has twice as many, which is two gee.

marks.giver: 2g − 3 is written for the larger herd
marks.taker: g + 3 is written for the smaller herd

beats.colours: giver and receiver in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='giver'/>Step two, move three cows. {{NAME_4}} is left with two gee take away three.
<bookmark mark='taker'/>{{NAME_3}} receives those three cows, and now has gee plus three.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Both herds are then equal. That gives two gee take away three, equal to gee plus three.

marks.add: 3 is added to both sides to give 2g = g + 6
marks.take: g is taken from both sides to give g = 6

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add three to both sides, and two gee is gee plus six.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Take gee from both sides, and gee is six.
<bookmark mark='big'/>Step four, check with six. {{NAME_4}} has two times six, which is twelve cows.
<bookmark mark='equal'/>After giving three, {{NAME_4}} has nine. {{NAME_3}} has six plus three, which is also nine.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_3}} has six cows and {{NAME_4}} has twelve.
